pull.title: KAFKA-21312: Implement snapshottable tasks in the coordinator runtime
pull.body:
When a write fails, the runtime reverts the coordinator state, but not
the tasks scheduled by the reverted write operations. When those tasks
complete, their results may no longer apply to the coordinator state.

Delay submitting the tasks scheduled by write operations until their
batch is written, and cancel them without submitting them if their batch
is reverted. Operations without records do not open a batch, so when no
batch is open, their tasks are submitted immediately rather than waiting
indefinitely for the next write. Cancelling a task is not reverted with
the operation which cancelled it. It is expected that callers
re-schedule tasks if they are still needed.

Do the same in MockCoordinatorExecutor and
GroupMetadataManagerTestContext, for use in future tests that roll back
writes which schedule tasks.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Reviewers: David Jacot <dajac@apache.org>, ChickenchickenLove
 <ojt90902@naver.com>

repo.name: kafka
repo.description: Apache Kafka - A distributed event streaming platform

review_comments.body: Have you considered the other way around? We could keep the new tasks as pending until the write succeeds. The benefit is that it would only use the executor when it is really decided.

That would be good for saving resources in the (less common) cases where reverts happen. We don't have any strong latency requirements for the tasks so it sounds okay. I tried it in the latest update to the PR. It's a little more complicated to test now that it's part of the task lifecycle.

How do we ensure that the tasks in currentBatchTasks belong to the batch being flushed?

An operation may schedule a task while generating its records, before `append()` is called. If `append()` then needs to flush the previous batc--for example, because the new records do not fit--could `onBatchWritten()` submit that task before its own records have been appended?

If the subsequent append fails, the task may already have been submitted even though the records it depends on were not written. Is there a guarantee that prevents this sequence, or do we need to associate the tasks more explicitly with their batch?

(I'm struggling with this in KAFKA-19023 as well. 😓 )

You've stumbled upon one of the bugs in https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/KAFKA-20912. It also impacts non-replaying operations which update the timeline structures directly.

We haven't decided how to fix it yet. One option could be to drop the flush-on-large-batch entirely. Another could be to create a snapshot after each append().

commit.message:
KAFKA-21312: Implement snapshottable tasks in the coordinator runtime

When a write fails, the runtime reverts the coordinator state, but not
the tasks scheduled by the reverted write operations. When those tasks
complete, their results may no longer apply to the coordinator state.

Have the executor take part in the coordinator state's snapshots.
Reverting to a snapshot now also cancels the tasks scheduled since that
snapshot. Tasks cancelled or completed since the snapshot are not
restored. It is expected that callers re-schedule them if they are
still needed.

Do the same in MockCoordinatorExecutor and
GroupMetadataManagerTestContext, for use in future tests that roll back
writes which schedule tasks.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

issue.title: KAFKA-19023: Implement snapshottable timers in the coordinator runtime

repository.name: kafka
repository.description: Apache Kafka - A distributed event streaming platform

issue.body:
This PoC makes `CoordinatorTimerImpl` snapshottable, aligning timer
state restoration with the Coordinator’s snapshot and rollback
lifecycle.

The main changes are:

1. `CoordinatorTimerImpl` stores a `TimerState` for each timer in a
`TimelineHashMap`, using the same `SnapshotRegistry` as the Coordinator.
2. `TimerState` contains the information needed to recreate a
`TimerTask`: its deadline, operation, and retry configuration. Scheduled
`TimerTask` instances are managed separately.
3. When a record append succeeds, the existing
`updateLastWrittenOffset(offset)` flow creates a snapshot at that
offset, including the timer state. Scheduled tasks continue running
unchanged.
4. If the append fails, `revertLastWrittenOffset()` restores the timer
state to the rollback target snapshot.
5. After restoring the state, `timer.onRollback()` cancels all currently
tracked tasks and schedules new tasks based on the restored `TimerState
entries`. Each task uses the time remaining until its original deadline,
or a delay of zero if the deadline has already passed

Reviewers: Sean Quah <squah@confluent.io>, David Jacot
 <dajac@apache.org>
